2.5.11.4 The Multi-Core-Module as Mappable Element
In this case the mappable element is again the MCAL module which can be mapped to at least one or multiple cores. The MCAL module itself is implemented according to multi-core type IV and applies one of the shown software separation strategies. However the service API are available on all cores the MCAL module is mapped to. The ISR of the MCAL module are ideally mapped to the core the user is running on. Typical MCAL modules are IO drivers required by any core implementing non atomic hardware elements, such as ADC, PWM, ICU, OCU and SPI. The resulting mapping rule is: A multi-core MCAL module can be mapped to any and even multiple cores. Consequently all hardware elements are mapped to all cores the MCAL module is used on.
